behavior: Flits and hops through shrubs and saplings, gleaning insects—especially from leaf undersides—and sometimes sallying after flying prey. Often raises its tail and droops its wings while foraging.
field_marks: Small, slim-bodied warbler with a relatively long tail, often held cocked.
Short, dark, pointed bill; dark round eye; slender gray legs.
Breeding adults have a yellow crown and black eye stripe framing a white cheek.
Breeding adults show a rich chestnut flank stripe against clean white underparts.
Dark wings bear two pale yellow wingbars; the dark tail has white outer feathers.
Nonbreeding adults and immatures are lime-olive above, with a pale gray face, crisp white eye-ring, and little or no chestnut.
habitat: Young deciduous regrowth, dense thickets, brushy forest edges, and overgrown fields; migrants and wintering birds also use a wider range of shrubby and forested habitats.
